verses.1: And after that, the serpent king of the people of Benyamin died. Then his son became king instead of him.
verses.2: And David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun, son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me. So David sent messengers to comfort his father. David’s servants went to the land of the people of Hanun to comfort him.”
verses.3: And the officials of the people of Amun said to Hanun, “David has killed your father before your eyes. He sent you here as a messenger, but in reality, his purpose was to explore and conquer the land. His servants came to you.”
verses.4: And Hanun took David’s servants, cut them off, and branded their cheeks with a mark that would last forever. Then he sent them away.
verses.5: And they went and told David about those people. Then he sent for them, so that they could be punished because those people had done very bad things. The king said, “Return to your homes until your elders are brought back to life.”
verses.6: And the sons of Ammon saw that David had arrived. So they sent Hanun and the sons of Ammon, along with thousands of gold coins, to hire men from the land of Canaan, from the land of Makhah and Tzobah.
verses.7: They hired two and three hundred thousand soldiers for them. They also hired King Maachah and his people. They came and camped before Midba. The people of Maachah gathered from their cities and went into battle.
verses.8: David heard this, and he sent Joab along with all the soldiers of the king’s army.
verses.9: And the sons of Amun went out to fight. They attacked the gates of the city and the kings who were standing there in the field.
verses.10: And Joab saw that the situation at the battle was favorable for him. He then chose from all the men in Israel, and prepared them to face Aram.
verses.11: And the rest of the people were given into the hands of Abshai, his brother. They were then appointed to govern the children of Amun.
verses.12: And he said, “If you become stronger than me, then Aram will be under your control, and you will be my savior. But if the sons of Ammon become stronger than you, then they will save you.”
verses.13: May it be strengthened and grow stronger for our people, and for the cities of our God. May He who is good in His eyes do this.
verses.14: And Joab and the people with him went before Aram to fight. They were defeated by them.
verses.15: And the sons of Ammon saw that Aram had been defeated. They also rushed forward from behind their brother Abshay. They entered the city, and Joab entered Jerusalem.
verses.16: And Aram saw that they were defeated before Israel. So they sent their magicians, and they brought out Aram’s army from across the river. And they poured out their army in front of them.
verses.17: And he went to David. He gathered all of Israel together. They crossed the Jordan River, and David went up to them. Then David prepared for battle against the Ammonites. They fought against them.
verses.18: And Aram attacked Israel. David killed seven thousand chariots and forty thousand infantrymen from Aram. Also, the leader of Aram was killed.
verses.19: And the servants of Hadadzer were afraid, for they had been defeated before Israel. They became friends with David and obeyed him. But Aram did not come to save the children of his people anymore.
